target_columns.name: claim_to_sum_insured_ratio
target_columns.transformation: claim_amount / sum_insured, rounded to 4 decimal places

target_columns.name: review_flag
target_columns.transformation: CASE on unrounded claim_amount/sum_insured: >=0.5 -> 'REVIEW REQUIRED', >=0.25 -> 'WATCH', else 'STANDARD'

quirks: review_flag thresholds (0.5, 0.25) are computed on the raw unrounded ratio, not the rounded claim_to_sum_insured_ratio column -- using the rounded value could flip borderline rows across a threshold
hardcoded magic-number thresholds 0.5 and 0.25 are not parameterised anywhere in the legacy job -- preserve as literal constants, do not infer config
INNER JOIN to policies silently drops any claim whose policy_id has no matching policy row (no LEFT JOIN null-handling, no fan-out expected if policy_id is unique per policy)

WHERE c.status <> 'Rejected' uses SQL not-equals semantics -- if status is NULL in source data, those rows are silently excluded (NULL <> 'Rejected' is NULL, not TRUE) and must NOT be reclassified as included in the PySpark port

division claim_amount / sum_insured has no explicit guard against sum_insured = 0 or NULL in the original SQL -- original behavior (NULL or divide-by-zero error depending on engine) must be preserved or explicitly documented as a deviation

output is ORDER BY claim_to_sum_insured_ratio DESC -- if downstream consumers depend on row order (e.g. top-N review queues), the PySpark job must replicate the sort, not just produce an unordered DataFrame
